class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus

audited_plan.image_description: The image shows a water surface with ripples. Two dark, textured objects are partially submerged. The object on the right is clearly the snout and upper head of a crocodilian, showing rough skin texture and a nostril. The object on the left appears to be another part of a crocodilian body or a second individual, showing similar armored texture. The rest of the bodies are submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible snout on the right exhibits a distinct tapering V-shape profile characteristic of crocodiles, contrasting with the broader U-shape of alligators. This geometric feature is clearly discernible despite partial submersion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the mouth is closed, the specific diagnostic feature of the fourth lower tooth fitting into the upper jaw notch (interlocking) is not clearly visible due to the angle and water line obscuring the precise jaw margin. Therefore, the 'interlocking' aspect cannot be confirmed as present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye region is obscured by the viewing angle and distance; pupil shape and nictitating membrane are impossible to verify at this resolution.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct nostril opening is visible at the very tip of the snout on the right-hand subject, consistent with crocodilian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portions of the subjects show a rough, armored texture consistent with crocodilian skin, and the linear arrangement suggests an elongated body form.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture on the visible back/snout areas shows the characteristic rugged, raised pattern of osteoderms/scutes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is dark grey/brown and the surface is visibly rough and non-reflective (matte), matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral surface (belly) is completely submerged and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs are visible above the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in the frame.
